sections.h2: What makes Ohio different for a home seller?
sections.html:
Ohio is a big state with several large metro areas, and the rules for taxes, probate, foreclosure and tenants come from state statute but are carried out by county offices. The state was admitted to the Union on March 1, 1803, its capital and largest city is Columbus, and its largest metro areas center on Cleveland, Cincinnati and Columbus. Ohio's land area is 40,858.76 square miles by the 2020 Census count, and the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate counts 11,900,510 people.

A seller in Toledo, Dayton, Akron or a small township faces one Revised Code but a different auditor, recorder, treasurer, probate court and clerk of courts in each county. The guides on this site follow that split: statewide topic pages cover the law, and city and county pages cover the offices.

sections.h2: How do Ohio property tax appeals and transfer charges work?
sections.html:
Valuation disputes start at the county auditor. Under R.C. 5715.19, an owner files a complaint against a parcel's valuation with the county auditor on or before March 31 of the following tax year, or the date the first-half collection closes if that is later, and the county board of revision hears it. A second complaint on the same parcel in the same interim period is barred unless an arm's length sale, a casualty loss, a substantial improvement or a change of at least fifteen percent in occupancy intervenes.

At closing, each county may levy a real property transfer tax of up to thirty cents per hundred dollars of value under R.C. 322.02. The grantor pays it to the county auditor before the deed goes to the recorder. Because counties set their own rates and many differ, the county page for the property is where to look.

sections.h2: How do Ohio probate, transfer on death deeds and foreclosure sales work?
sections.html:
Ohio estates go through the probate court that serves the decedent's home county. A court may release a small estate from administration when assets total $35,000 or less, or $100,000 or less when everything goes to a surviving spouse (R.C. 2113.03). Executors and administrators sell land under R.C. 2127.01 through 2127.43. The Ohio estate tax was repealed for deaths on or after January 1, 2013, and the Department of Taxation says the 2021 sunset ended collection on older estates too.

Owners can also record a transfer on death designation affidavit with the county recorder, which vests title in named beneficiaries at death (R.C. 5302.22).

Foreclosure in Ohio is a court process. R.C. 2323.07 says that when a mortgage is foreclosed, a sale of the property shall be ordered by the court, which may direct the officer to sell in parcels or as a whole, and may name the sheriff or master of each county where the land lies. A homeowner who wants to avoid a sale has to act before the court orders it.

sections.h2: How do landlord and tenant rules affect selling a rented Ohio house?
sections.html:
Selling with a tenant in the house adds a notice calendar and a court calendar. Ohio requires at least three days of written notice before filing an eviction (R.C. 1923.04), thirty days before a periodic rental date to end a month-to-month tenancy (R.C. 5321.17), and a court hearing no sooner than the seventh day after service. Landlords cannot lock out tenants or shut off utilities (R.C. 5321.15).

  • The state topic pages on eviction notice and eviction process lay out the notice types and the court stages.
  • The landlord-tenant page covers deposits, repairs and retaliation.
  • Rented-house sellers should read both before setting a closing date.

sections.h2: Which Ohio county office handles which step?
sections.html:
Ohio splits property work across several county offices, which is why a statewide rule can produce a different experience in each county.

  • County auditor: property valuation complaints, and the transfer tax paid at deed delivery.
  • County recorder: deeds, transfer on death affidavits and recorded liens.
  • County treasurer: tax bills and payment of property tax.
  • Probate court: estates, release from administration and land sales by fiduciaries.
  • Municipal or county court clerk: eviction filings and summons service.
  • Sheriff: carries out writs and foreclosure sales ordered by the common pleas court.

Ask each office for its current fee schedule and forms, since those change more often than the statutes.

sections.h2: What does Ohio's land and housing mix mean for a sale?
sections.html:
The state covers 40,858.76 square miles of land and 288.8 people per square mile by the 2020 count, which puts dense city blocks in Cleveland and Columbus alongside farm townships. Mean travel time to work is 23.4 minutes for Ohio workers aged 16 and over, a figure that shapes how far buyers will look from a job center.

Ohio's median monthly owner costs run $1,517 with a mortgage and $588 without one, and the median gross rent is $1,034. Those numbers frame what a buyer or a landlord can carry. Sellers with a property that needs work often weigh a cash sale against the cost and delay of repairs before listing.

  • Dense counties usually have more recorded sales to support a valuation complaint.
  • Rural counties may have fewer comparable sales, so a tax appeal can rest on property condition.
  • Cities add their own permits and codes on top of state law, so check city hall as well as the county.

sections.h2: How should I use the Ohio guides on this site?
sections.html: Begin with the statewide topic page that matches the problem, such as probate, foreclosure, eviction or estate tax, then move to the county or city guide for the house itself. County recorder guides cover deed recording, property tax guides cover the auditor and treasurer, and city pages cover local selling conditions. If a situation spans topics, such as an inherited rental with a tenant, read the probate and eviction pages together.

faqs.q: What is the latest population estimate for Ohio?
faqs.a: About 11.9 million. The Census Bureau lists 11,900,510 for mid-2025, a rise of 0.9 percent from its April 2020 estimates base.

faqs.q: What share of Ohio homes are owner-occupied?
faqs.a: 67.2 percent for 2020 to 2024, according to the Census Bureau, and the median value of those homes is $214,800.

faqs.q: Where do I file a property valuation complaint in Ohio?
faqs.a: With the county auditor, by March 31 of the following tax year or the close of first-half collection if later. The county board of revision then hears it, under R.C. 5715.19.

faqs.q: Is there a statewide transfer tax on Ohio home sales?
faqs.a: The tax is county-based. R.C. 322.02 lets each county levy a real property transfer tax of up to thirty cents per hundred dollars, paid by the grantor to the county auditor. Ask the county auditor for the current rate.

faqs.q: Does Ohio still have an estate tax?
faqs.a: No. The Ohio Department of Taxation says the estate tax was repealed for deaths on or after January 1, 2013, and that no tax is due on property first discovered after December 31, 2021.
